ranked.headline: Quantum learning models sidestep noise and concentration via ensembles, calibration, fixed maps
ranked.summary: Recent preprints target noise and exponential concentration in parametrized quantum models with boosting, reusable calibration and training-free feature maps.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is keeping quantum machine learning trainable under hardware noise and exponential concentration. One route replaces or supplements error mitigation. Boosting of noisy parametrized circuits is compared against probabilistic error cancellation and found to need fewer resources. Bagging and AdaBoost are applied to variational regressors. A reusable calibration framework restores QNN convergence. A learned small-circuit mitigator combined with circuit cutting outperforms ZNE and Clifford-based methods on larger circuits. A second route limits variational optimization: Soft-MoQE classically gates fixed quantum feature maps and matches trainable QNNs on MNIST. Riemannian-gradient schemes avoid measurement and classical feedback, and a quantum Transformer is trained via multi-agent RL without backpropagation. An empirical study links entanglement, locality and bandwidth scaling to concentration in quantum kernels and extreme learning. Contractive layers with one trainable parameter add expressivity on Rydberg arrays. Applications include end-to-end b/c-jet tagging on a 5-qubit superconducting processor and Dempster-Shafer uncertainty-aware classification. All works are preprints.

ranked.headline: DESI-era data test whether dark energy evolves, crosses the phantom divide, or clusters
ranked.summary: New reconstructions, model comparisons and independent SN Ia pipelines probe the DESI-driven w0–wa departure from ΛCDM and its systematics.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is whether DESI BAO or full-shape data, combined with CMB, supernova and lensing probes, require dark energy beyond a cosmological constant. Within VCDM, three one-parameter vacuum histories are compared. F42 is favored by AIC when supernovae are included, while Bayesian evidence is assessed separately. A DESI DR1 full-shape analysis finds that the scalar-field Fading Dark Sector model outperforms CPL w0–wa. Two non-parametric reconstructions of the effective dark-energy density and gravitational response report a phantom-divide crossing near z≈0.5–0.7. One of them also asks whether dark energy clusters. A proposed set of 0i Einstein-equation tests uses observables alone to separate gravity, dark energy and dark matter. On supernova systematics, LEMAITRE and a ZTF/SNLS/HSC calibration effort provide independent SN Ia data to test the w–w_a tension. A forecast asks whether Simons Observatory and CMB-S4 can distinguish w0waCDM from ΛCDM shadow models. Separate preprints address 21 cm signatures of boosted dark matter and the effect of astrophysical priors on pulsar-timing-array evidence for new physics.

ranked.headline: Quantum compilers optimize physical cost: atom transport, pulse latency, coupling limits
ranked.summary: Compilers now optimize atom transport, pulse latency and routing directly, as QEC simulators add ion heating, coherent noise and mid-circuit measurement.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is compilation scored by platform-level cost rather than abstract gate count. NEAT optimizes AOD-based atom transport, placement, routing and scheduling for neutral-atom arrays. SCOPE uses an operator Schmidt time surrogate to cut pulse execution latency and reports gains over EPOC on 104 benchmarks. The quspect SDK selects routings after coupling-constrained resynthesis, using 0.616x the two-qubit gates of Qiskit O3 on 55 circuits. CAVQS and a persistent-occupancy compiler for independent-set problems add synthesis and constraint-preserving structure. A second thread makes QEC simulation more hardware-realistic. THeatA tracks per-ion phonon numbers under QCCD transport. Compiled Clifford-augmented MPS reach distance-9 surface codes under coherent noise. MASQ provides exact near-Clifford sampling, and pre-trajectory GPU sampling now handles general Kraus channels and mid-circuit measurements. GEARS uses syndrome feedback with gate-error amplification for in-situ recalibration, reducing measurement needs about eightfold.

ranked.headline: Dynamics expose hidden nonlocal entanglement in open, driven and quenched quantum systems
ranked.summary: Preprints track how long-range and multipartite entanglement persist under decoherence, Floquet driving and quenches, and shape late-time observables.
ranked.synthesis: The main thread is the use of time evolution to reveal nonlocal quantum structure that local or static probes miss. A decoherence-driven transition from a 1D SPT state to a trivial product state carries hidden long-range correlations. Floquet drives that proliferate fermionic anyons in the toric code leave a long-time state with long-range entanglement, presented as a Floquet analog of mixed-state topological order. In crosscap states, local symmetry breaking grows while entanglement decreases, because the asymmetry is initially encoded in long-range entanglement. Crystal quenches in a tight-binding chain show configurations with no irreducible tripartite entanglement. Charged dual-unitary circuits with a symmetry-breaking impurity display non-monotonic entropy growth. Open-system work extracts a non-Hermitian Lindbladian invariant from covariance-matrix relaxation and links graph spectra to late-time qubit concurrence. Two complementary studies connect chaos onset in spin ladders, and the QMC sign problem, to entanglement and nonstabilizerness.

ranked.headline: Emulators and field-level models speed nonlinear predictions for LSST, DESI and FRB cosmology
ranked.summary: New emulators, differentiable bispectra and field-level Lyman-α models target the accuracy and speed demanded by LSST Year 1 and DESI DR2-era analyses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is fast, accurate theory and forward modeling for upcoming survey analyses. A Hi-COLA-trained emulator provides the nonlinear matter power spectrum in Cubic Galileon gravity, validated for LSST Year 1 weak lensing and clustering. bihalofit-JAX delivers a differentiable nonlinear bispectrum and projected statistics, reported to run orders of magnitude faster. For the Lyman-α forest, a cubic-order EFT field-level forward model validated on CAMELS and Sherwood yields BAO shift predictions and simulation-based priors, while a 3D U-Net maps density and velocity to flux, reproducing P1D, bispectrum and trispectrum across TNG and FLAMINGO. A secondary thread exploits alternative probes. Fast radio bursts give a first Ωm–w inference from 125 localized events alone, and, with IllustrisTNG, constraints on Ω_b f_ion across large-scale structure. A physics-informed neural network reconstructs w and the growth index from DESI DR2 to test GR, and Padé cosmography is forecast for LISA, ET and DECIGO sirens. The QCD equation-of-state study is peripheral.

ranked.headline: Real-time decoders, Pauli frame tracking and verified compilers co-designed for fault-tolerant control stacks
ranked.summary: New preprints push sub-microsecond QEC feedback, multi-GPU decoding and FPGA decoder evaluation, alongside verified compilers and speculative execution for FTQC.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the classical stack that must keep pace with fault-tolerant quantum hardware. On decoding, Pêlagos orchestrates relay belief-propagation across multiple GPUs under real-time constraints, and a survey organizes hierarchical decoding by decoder- and code-level hierarchy, platforms and latency trade-offs. CHEQ evaluates decoders concurrently on an FPGA by geometric-skip circuit-level noise sampling, matching Stim firing rates within 0.16%. QuFrame closes the QEC loop within 1 μs through real-time Pauli frame tracking. Froq proposes safe speculative execution on live quantum states using compiler-assisted recovery contracts. A second strand addresses platform-specific compilation and control: an FPGA-based quantum data processing unit for neutral-atom arrays with NVQLink round-trip measurements, Lean-verified QCCD co-design scaling to 512 qubits, a machine-checked simulation compiler, and fidelity-predictive multi-vendor QPU scheduling.

ranked.headline: Scalable classical and quantum algorithms for simulation, sensing, search and analog optimization
ranked.summary: Eight preprints pair classical simulation limits with task-specific quantum algorithms for sensing, search, sampling and Ising optimization.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is algorithm-level analysis of where quantum or analog hardware offers advantage and where classical methods suffice. On the classical side, F2-linear partitioning scales Pauli propagation beyond 10^11 Pauli strings, and window propagation gives a provably polynomial-time approximation of first-order OTOCs in 1D Haar-random brickwork circuits. On the quantum side, task-specific sensing algorithms achieve a sqrt(N) speedup for discrete-frequency spectroscopy, and a unified framework for AC field sensing reports pulse protocols that beat dynamical decoupling. Hardware-facing work includes a gate-based realization of deterministic quantum-walk search, a photonic scheme for fluid-flow modeling, and an opto-electronic Ising machine with 100,000 spins read out in a single shot. A complexity analysis of bosonic Lindbladian fixed points addresses stationary-state estimation and sampling.

ranked.headline: Structured leakage, loss and correlated noise are characterized and exploited in error correction
ranked.summary: Experiments and simulators now resolve correlated noise, leakage and loss in QEC, tying characterized noise to code geometry, circuits and mitigation.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread treats non-ideal hardware noise in error correction and mitigation as structured and measurable rather than idealized Pauli noise. A 105-qubit superconducting experiment scales surface-code stability tests to 7x7 patches and identifies temporally correlated heating-to-|3> leakage. Foliated surface codes are shown to be optimal against space- and time-like skip-gate leakage, and Ellis provides fast Pauli-frame simulation under qubit loss and leakage. Logical error prediction under biased circuit-level noise guides rectangular surface-code geometry selection, cutting qubit overhead. Magic state cultivation with lattice-surgery escapes is demonstrated on IBM hardware. Near-term work extends bnZNE mitigation to randomized circuits and proposes a self-baseline testing oracle with a controlled false-positive rate. The common novelty is linking characterized noise to code design, resource choices and validation.

ranked.headline: Quantum reservoirs gain nonlinearity via re-uploading and dephasing; learned models infer Hamiltonians
ranked.summary: Preprints probe how encoding, dephasing and readout set memory and nonlinearity in quantum reservoirs, alongside recurrent and learned models for Hamiltonian inference.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how input encoding, noise and readout determine computational capacity in fixed-dynamics quantum models. Data re-uploading is reported to improve higher-order nonlinear processing and chaotic-series tasks in physical reservoirs. Two spin-chain studies treat dephasing as a resource: one simulates a six-qubit reservoir where dephasing and observable choice affect NARMA, limit-cycle and chaotic forecasting, the other proposes a minimum-complexity open XX chain with pure dephasing. Multi-layer quantum extreme learning machines with MMD-fitted linear readouts are proposed for generative modeling, while variational quantum recurrent networks are benchmarked for memory and nonlinear capacity against classical baselines. Adjacent work applies recurrent quantum RL and JEPA-based world models to Hamiltonian identification, and randomized real-time dynamics to neural-network quantum states.

ranked.headline: Nonreciprocity and tunable coupling are being engineered in compact photonic, magnonic and metasurface platforms
ranked.summary: Preprints pair nonreciprocal isolators and Floquet metasurfaces with tunable magnonic, ENZ and THz platforms for compact control of optical response.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is control of wave response beyond static, reciprocal behavior in compact geometries. Two items address nonreciprocity directly: a computational study of integrated isolators based on nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors with spin-momentum locking, including an all-optical isolator proposal, and Floquet metasurfaces of three closely spaced conducting sheets that show asymmetric frequency conversion and a reported violation of Kirchhoff's law. Tunability appears elsewhere: a CrCl3 tripartite van der Waals cavity magnonic device with hierarchical anti-crossing and reduced magnon loss, VCMA-driven parametric spin-wave excitation with two phase states, high-Q THz flatbands in Mie-grating metasurfaces, and inverse-designed epsilon-near-zero oxide cavities with stronger confinement. A review covers strain-driven THz phase modulation. The items differ in method and maturity (computational, theoretical, experimental) and do not share one mechanism; the acoustic bound-state study is a wave-physics analogue.

ranked.headline: qLDPC decoders trade off accuracy and latency via parallel, adaptive and GPU methods
ranked.summary: Eight preprints from mid-November 2026 push qLDPC decoding toward real-time accuracy, alongside code designs for fixed-connectivity hardware.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is decoding quantum LDPC codes at high accuracy within real-time budgets. SCOPE, a physics-informed parallel decoder, reports a logical error rate of 4.82e-10 on the [[144,12,12]] BB code with 173.8 ns latency. TEMPO-BP adapts per-variable memory strength through local feedback and lowers logical failure rates versus BP+OSD and Relay-BP. TCBP-JOBS learns calibrated fault probabilities on GPUs and matches Tesseract accuracy. A hybrid sliding-window decoder for trapped-ion noise uses soft-output confidence to switch windows, outperforming BP-LSD. Parity push post-selection rejects unreliable shots in a decoder-agnostic way, and non-binary detector error models improve belief propagation under circuit-level noise. Code design contributes Armillary codes with rates above 1/2 for fixed-connectivity superconducting hardware and rate-optimal distance-3 and distance-4 color codes.

ranked.headline: Simulations quantify how modelling systematics bias cosmological parameters from lensing, clustering and tSZ
ranked.summary: Eight preprints use simulations and mocks to size parameter biases from n(z), lens multipoles, light-cone effects and halo bias ahead of Euclid-class and DESI analyses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of simulations and mocks to quantify how astrophysical and modelling systematics propagate into cosmological inference. Euclid-like 3×2pt analyses show that n(z) errors bias w0wa, motivating on-the-fly Gaussian Process reconstruction. IllustrisTNG ellipticals show multipole mass terms bias time-delay H0 by 1–6%. Light-cone and relativistic effects shift local fNL by about 2σ (Euclid-like) and over 10σ (MegaMapper-like). On the bias side, TNG300 links halo secondary bias largely to unbound circum-halo matter, luminosity-weighted marked correlations are proposed as an assembly-bias null test on DESI-BGS mocks, and the hybrid Lagrangian expansion is extended to post-reconstruction clustering. Baryonification V produces tSZ Compton-y maps from dark-matter-only light cones. The DESI Legacy cluster test of general relativity is a more peripheral item.

ranked.headline: Inference pipelines for GW, lensing, clustering and 21-cm data are built and benchmarked
ranked.summary: Eight November 2026 preprints report samplers, simulators and ML tools, plus an SKA challenge, preparing inference for LISA, Euclid, LSST and SKA data.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the construction and validation of inference infrastructure for forthcoming cosmological datasets, though not every item concerns sampler efficiency. ASPIRE reuses existing posteriors for joint dark-siren cosmological and population inference, reporting 6-28x speedups over reanalysis. samsara++ implements trans-dimensional MCMC in C++/CUDA for LISA global fits of overlapping Galactic binaries and noise. The LSST DESC cluster pipeline is validated on cosmoDC2 mocks, constraining Omega_c and sigma_8. Euclid work addresses ML components: strong-lens detection depends strongly on training-set composition, image format and ensembling, while EuclidFM learns 128-dim embeddings from Q1 photometry. SciPIC-lite offers a public HOD library for clustering observables. A differentiable GPU-accelerated 21-cm forward model targets uncertainty quantification, and SKA SDC3b finds inter-team variability among 16 EoR pipelines.

ranked.headline: Symmetry-derived optical, transport and magnon probes proposed for unconventional magnets
ranked.summary: Eight preprints link altermagnetic, odd-parity and spin-nematic order to concrete probes: magneto-optics, spin photocurrent, charge-spin transport and thermal Hall.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is theory that connects measurable responses to the symmetry of unconventional magnetic order. For altermagnets, noncoplanar antiferromagnets and odd-parity magnets, the proposed probes are octupolar magneto-optical effects, nonlinear spin generation and spin photocurrent, and charge-spin selection rules with temporal-spectral separation in transport. Twist engineering of collinear bilayers is proposed to yield quasicrystalline altermagnets with high-order spin polarization. On the magnon side, single magnons and bound magnon pairs in pyrochlore spin-nematics give competing thermal Hall contributions, allowing field-tunable sign reversal. In CrI3 nanotubes, an axial field produces a conical phase and a large pseudo-orbital magnon moment. In BiFeO3, gate-controlled domain boundaries modulate nonreciprocal magnons in a proposed transistor. Cavity photon condensation driven by scalar spin chirality is more peripheral. All eight are preprints.

ranked.headline: Coupled and reconfigurable resonances in metasurfaces, microresonators and nanoantennas tune optical response
ranked.summary: Seven preprints report quantified resonance control via strong coupling, vapor-driven anion exchange and material choice across dielectric, perovskite, plasmonic and 2D platforms.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is engineering resonant response through mode coupling, composition or environment. Silicon BIC metasurfaces use QBIC-GMR strong coupling for intrinsic circular dichroism of 0.995 at 1653.9 nm (Q = 1083). Bulk WS2 metasurfaces reach polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling between Brillouin-zone-folding quasi-BICs and A excitons. MAPbBr3 BIC resonances tune reversibly and continuously under HCl/HBr vapor anion exchange, and coupled TiO2 and perovskite-coated microresonators show non-monotonic whispering gallery mode hybridization. Plasmonic nanoantenna arrays with hollow-core fiber coupling report 2.1 mW THz output and 145 dB dynamic range, while a theoretical coaxial nanoantenna study maps inverse Faraday magnetization across five materials. MXene-derived TiO2 polarizers (FOM 17.5) add an integrated-photonics route. New here is the breadth of quantified tuning mechanisms; several results are numerical or theoretical.

ranked.headline: Theory models for tracer cross-correlations and dark energy tested against simulations
ranked.summary: Six preprints test EFT, halo-model and dark-energy mapping prescriptions against simulations, supporting 21 cm, Lyα, SPHEREx and field-level analyses.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is validating theoretical prescriptions against simulations before applying them to data. Two Lyman-alpha works test EFT descriptions: a minimal tree-level model for 21 cm and Lyα auto- and cross-spectra at z=2.4-4.2, constraining HI and Lyα biases, and a power spectrum plus bispectrum full-shape analysis on AbacusSummit mocks at z=2.5 for DESI. The SPHEREx pair forecasts extragalactic background light cross-correlated with CMB lensing, with the second paper reporting halo-model predictions consistent with lightcone simulations. Two further papers show that N-body runs with constant w can reproduce CPL and general w(z) dark energy at the field level by matching the expansion history, with power spectra agreeing within 0.2% in one case. New here is the combination of line-intensity, forest, lensing and simulation-mapping validation.

ranked.headline: Quantum geometry, disorder and interactions shape Hall responses and magnetism in topological and flat-band systems
ranked.summary: Six preprints from mid-November 2026 tie Hall plateaus, anomalous Hall metals and nonlinear transport to quantum geometry, disorder and interactions.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how band geometry, interactions and disorder determine Hall-type and related transport responses in topological and narrow-band materials. Studies address layer-dependent disorder controlling integer and fractional Chern plateau widths in twisted bilayer MoTe2, quantum geometry enabling altermagnetic and nematic order in narrow bands, and interaction-driven pseudospin order with anomalous Hall metals in Bernal-stacked tetralayer graphene. Others extend transport theory: multi-Weyl magnetotransport beyond the constant relaxation-time approximation, quantum-geometric nonlinear conductivity in SrTiO3 electron gases comparing (001) and (111) interfaces, and a 3D quantum anomalous Hall system where Chern numbers alone fail to characterize chiral responses. The new element is treating geometry and realistic disorder or interactions as explicit determinants of response. All six are preprints and theoretical or numerical in the summaries given.

ranked.headline: Neural estimators replace likelihood and quadratic pipelines across cosmological inference tasks
ranked.summary: Five preprints in one week apply neural posterior, map-level, transformer and generative methods to FRB, CMB, kSZ and gravitational-wave cosmology inference.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the substitution of neural, simulation-trained estimators for conventional analytic or sampling-based steps in cosmological inference. AttNPE recovers FRB cosmology posteriors matching MCMC at roughly 10^6 lower cost. A spherical graph CNN infers r directly from multifrequency B-mode maps, beating a bandpower likelihood on RMSE and intervals. Simulation-based inference reconstructs first-order electroweak phase transition parameters from stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds. Vision Transformers outperform quadratic estimators in kSZ velocity reconstruction fidelity. Wavelet-CFM generates jointly correlated lensing, kSZ, tSZ and CIB maps, matching validation statistics. What is new is the breadth: neural methods now span posterior estimation, map-level inference, field reconstruction and simulation generation, with interpretability (AttNPE) and benchmarks against standard estimators as recurring elements.

ranked.headline: Learned and empirical mappings link dark matter halos to galaxies, gas and lensing mass maps
ranked.summary: Five preprints apply ML and empirical halo-galaxy models from z~2.3 protoclusters to z>6 JWST galaxies, in both forward and inverse directions.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the use of simulation-trained or empirical models to link dark matter structure to baryonic observables. In the forward direction, Extremely Randomized Trees and Gaussian Processes populate the 2.8 Gpc FLAMINGO-10k dark-matter-only run with a galaxy catalogue. An empirical model predicts individual halo concentrations from assembly histories in cold and warm dark matter over z=0-5. A flexible model connecting halo mass, stellar mass, SFR and UV magnitude is fit to JWST UV luminosity functions and angular correlations at z>6. In the inverse direction, deep learning infers cluster mass maps and subhalo substructure from HST imaging, matching CLASH lensing, and a CNN reconstructs IGM column-density maps from noisy KCWI Lyα cubes of z~2.3 protoclusters. The new element is the span of scales, redshifts and observables, though methods and targets differ across the items.

ranked.headline: Disorder and defects generate and tune orbital Hall and magnetoelectric responses
ranked.summary: Preprints show disorder and point defects can generate, enhance or tune orbital responses, while a clean-limit MoS2 study isolates orbital exchange effects.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that disorder and defects act as sources or tuning knobs for orbital transport rather than mere perturbations. Kubo-Bastin Chebyshev calculations on a centrosymmetric sp3 square lattice address robustness and tunability of an orbital Hall effect with quadrupole origin under disorder. Structural and electrostatic disorder, including amorphous graphene, is reported to produce sizable orbital Hall currents absent in pristine systems. A real-space study finds that point defects enhance and activate magnetoelectric orbital responses in a metallic orbital antiferromagnet. Two items differ in scope: the toroidal spin texture work treats dipole-dipole interaction landscapes in a classical magnetostatic model, and the MoS2 study derives intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity from an orbital exchange field without spin magnetism or spin-orbit coupling.

ranked.headline: Euclid DR1 near-infrared, astrometric and spectroscopic calibration chains
ranked.summary: Euclid DR1 papers document calibration and processing performance at release scale, measured against stated requirements.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the instrument-level processing and calibration that underlies Euclid DR1. The near-infrared processing function converts raw NISP observations into data products, and a companion paper details NIR astrometric calibration, including distortion modelling and residuals against Gaia DR3 reaching 30 mas. Ground-based optical imaging covering about 2500 deg2 provides colours, with photometric stability and depth validated for photo-z and PSF calibration. SIR spectroscopic calibration pipelines model the focal plane globally to meet wavelength and flux requirements. A calibration strategy paper reviews plan design, implementation and performance against requirements, including corrections for flux, astrometry, PSF, shear and wavelength. What is new is the documented performance of these chains at DR1 scale. The items describe pipelines and validation rather than cosmological constraints.

ranked.headline: Resonant cavities shape coherent light through nonlinear and modulated interactions
ranked.summary: Recent preprints demonstrate resonant light control in cryogenic silicon, gain-assisted fiber and modulated optomechanical platforms.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of resonant cavities to shape coherent light through nonlinear or modulated interactions. A passive silicon microring at 4.5 K sustains telecom-band optical parametric oscillation under a single continuous-wave pump, with a reported 2.25 mW onset. Two gain-assisted electro-optic fiber ring resonators with intracavity modulation produce a 1.8 THz flat-top comb for dual-comb spectroscopy. Intensity-modulated driving near mechanical resonance extends optomechanical oscillation amplitude and comb bandwidth toward the cavity-bandwidth limit. A thin-film lithium-niobate oscillator reports a roughly 100-fold enhanced thermal frequency coefficient, while a 60-cm in-vacuum Zerodur cavity addresses atom interferometry stability rather than light generation. What is new is the demonstration of these processes in specific platforms: cryogenic passive silicon, gain-assisted electro-optic fiber cavities, and modulated optomechanical systems.

ranked.headline: Extended symmetries reshape topological phase classification and invariant construction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend protecting symmetries to subsystem, half-chiral, and single-reflection settings, with new invariants for hinge and valley modes.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a focus on how symmetry structure constrains and classifies topological phases. The SymTFT review frames generalized symmetries, anomalies, and many-body phase classification within a single field-theoretic setting. Lattice response theory for subsystem SPT phases links response actions to cluster entanglers. Other works extend the protecting symmetry itself: an intrinsic chiral higher-order phase in a quarter-plane is stabilized by a single diagonal reflection, and half-chiral symmetry protects phases in which chiral symmetry acts on one sublattice only, characterized by real-space invariants. A generalized spectral localizer unifies Z and Z2 invariants for hinge modes, Dirac nodes, and valley boundary modes. The new element is the widening of protecting symmetries and invariants rather than a single shared method, so the dominant thread is symmetry-constrained classification across heterogeneous lattice and continuum settings.

ranked.headline: Switchable ferroelectric and magnetic order tunes excitons and valley states in 2D
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show ferroelectric, magnetic and optical order switching exciton and valley states in van der Waals bilayers and heterostructures.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is using an ordered degree of freedom as an external handle on excitonic and valley states in van der Waals materials. In rhombohedrally stacked bilayer WSe2, sliding ferroelectricity gives electrically switchable, hysteretic exciton photoluminescence and Raman response, and in few-layer R-stacked WSe2 it switches dipolar exciton transport and drives dipole reconfiguration toward quadrupolar excitons. In WS2/CrSBr heterostructures, type-II band alignment and magnetic-proximity Zeeman splitting couple valley and magnetic excitons. In WSe2/CrPS4, a light-controlled Néel vector switches valley polarization optically via spin-polarized charge transfer. The NbOCl2 preprint reports reversible room-temperature antiferroelectric switching probed by SHG and is the least directly tied to exciton or valley readout among the items. What is new is the breadth of switchable order, magnetic, ferroelectric and optical, applied to valley and exciton control.

ranked.headline: Strain and gates tune graphene valley, flat-band and superlattice states
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show strain-induced pseudo-fields and gate-defined superlattices now serve as design parameters for valley and correlated states.
ranked.synthesis: Three of the four preprints control the low-energy electronic structure of graphene through mechanical strain or electrostatic gating. In wrinkled graphene nanoribbons, tight-binding and quantum transport calculations show gate-tunable valley filtering and splitting. In multilayer graphene with rhombohedral stacking, strain generates giant pseudo-electric fields that produce flat bands, enhanced correlations, and topological boundary states. In Bernal bilayer graphene, a patterned graphite gate defines a superlattice with miniband insulating states and electrostatically tunable band structure. The twisted bilayer Floquet study addresses valley polarization and Chern-number phase transitions through periodic driving rather than strain or gating. The new element is the use of strain-induced pseudo-fields and gate-defined superlattices as design parameters for valley and correlated states. The items do not establish a single mechanism across the systems, so the shared thread is control of band structure rather than a unified physical picture.

ranked.headline: Learned and stochastic methods advance diffractive imaging and optical design
ranked.summary: Preprints now apply stochastic optimisation, residual learning and wave-coupled networks to ptychography and diffractive optical design.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the coupling of learned or stochastic optimisation with explicit wave-optical physics in diffractive imaging and optics design. Stochastic gradient descent for X-ray ptychographic reconstruction reports peak GPU memory at 65% and time at 22% of a baseline, targeting computational scalability of phase retrieval. An EUV ptychography study applies residual learning trained on physics simulations to restore diffraction patterns, reporting an edge-response width of about 1.08 μm at 57 nm. On the design side, multiscale wave-coupled neural networks (MSWNets) combine fully connected networks with Rayleigh-Sommerfeld propagation in a PINN-inspired inverse-design formulation for broadband diffractive optics. A further preprint extends surrogate-guided design to incoherent multispectral diffractive optical networks for satellite image classification, a task distinct from reconstruction. What is new across these works is the embedding of propagation physics directly into the learning or optimisation loop.

ranked.headline: Physics-based simulation and hybrid quantum models for learning hardware
ranked.summary: Four November 2026 preprints assess photonic and quantum learning hardware through simulation, functional evaluation, hybrid circuits, and qubit tuning.
ranked.synthesis: All four items are preprints linking learning architectures to physically grounded hardware models, the dominant thread being that device physics and functional performance are evaluated together. PISim couples DNN workloads with physics-based models of photonic accelerators, modulators, and laser sources for cross-layer design-space exploration. A separate proposal evaluates optical neural network modules against performance-matched digital replacements using an expressivity-based, function-oriented methodology. On the quantum side, hybrid PointNet-quantum networks with five QFT circuit configurations are assessed for LiDAR classification, while an FPGA-in-the-loop gradient descent system autonomously tunes spin qubits in electrostatically defined quantum dots. The novelty lies in closed-loop, hardware-aware assessment of learning systems; the available summaries report no quantitative comparisons across these approaches.

ranked.headline: Polarization, spatial and single-photon methods for multidimensional optical control
ranked.summary: Four November 2026 preprints report multidimensional optical encoding, sensing and wavefront control, with quantitative accuracy and delivery figures.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is the use of multiple optical degrees of freedom, including spatial, temporal, spectral and polarization information, to encode or recover information beyond simple intensity. One preprint reconstructs 2D and 3D fiber shape from a single end using picosecond time-resolved single-photon returns on a 32x32 SPAD array. Another stores data in polarized light within laser-induced nanostructures, reporting 99.45% raw accuracy. A third uses gradient metasurface pixels to convert spectral and polarization content into spatial patterns for snapshot infrared sensing. The fourth applies a phase-only MEMS modulator with 8,192 elements at 250 kHz refresh to wavefront shaping through multimode fiber, reporting 70% light delivery. The applications differ, so the dominant thread is multidimensional optical readout and control rather than a single method. The new element across the set is the pairing of single-photon time resolution, fast phase modulation and pixelated polarization-spectral encoding.

ranked.headline: Superconducting and quantum-dot platforms target spin and charge transport
ranked.summary: Recent preprints connect superconductivity with spin-to-charge conversion, quantized transport and thermometry in nanoscale devices.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the coupling of superconducting phase coherence to charge, spin and thermal transport in nanoscale devices. A gate-tunable superconducting quantum point contact in Ge/SiGe, probed with a SQUID, shows correlated quantization in conductance and switching current. A moiré flatband superconductor in alternating twisted trilayer graphene is linked to quantum phase fluctuations between superconductivity and bosonic phases. A two-orbital quantum dot Josephson junction with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and Zeeman splitting is proposed to convert a temperature difference into a phase difference for thermometry. A theoretical proposal argues that the inverse spin Hall effect in a superconductor could approach unity spin-to-charge conversion in a nonlocal spin-valve geometry. All four items are preprints, and the multiorbital and spin-conversion items are theoretical proposals.

ranked.headline: Computational schemes for energy spectra in semiconductors, quantum dots and solids
ranked.summary: Four preprints from mid-November 2026 extend spectral and electronic-structure methods to trions, magnetically confined systems and long-range Hamiltonians.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is numerical computation of energy spectra and electronic states in quantum systems, with emphasis on basis construction and solver design. Two items address confined or low-dimensional settings: a field-adaptive Hermite discrete variable representation benchmarked on two-dimensional quantum dots in perpendicular fields against analytic spectra, and a finite-element and Gaussian expansion treatment of trion energy levels in bulk semiconductors across hole-to-electron mass ratios. The remaining two items concern electronic structure in extended materials. One integrates a Krylov-based quantum impurity solver, with adaptive circuits and machine-learned moment prediction, into charge self-consistent DFT+QDMFT, validated on bcc systems. The other introduces MLEH-LR, a machine-learning electronic Hamiltonian that adds long-range interactions and external fields, applied to boron nitride ribbons. What is new across the set is the extension of established spectral approaches to external fields, long-range terms and learned components, rather than a single shared physical model.

ranked.headline: Programmable unitary interferometers for photonic computing, measurement and filtering
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend programmable unitary interferometers to optical neural networks, modular processors, and on-chip spectral measurement.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is the use of programmable interferometric networks as functional primitives in photonics. arXiv:2611.20390 proposes a logarithmic-depth butterfly interferometer architecture for parameter-efficient unitary transformations in coherent optical neural networks. arXiv:2611.21582 composes a modular processor from unitary tiles of fixed mixers and programmable phases, evaluated by numerical fitting. arXiv:2611.23667 uses unequal path lengths between two 8x8 unitary circuits on a universal silicon chip to achieve simultaneous spectral measurement and programmable filtering at 0.05 nm resolution. arXiv:2611.29115 instead realizes reconfigurable microwave photonic all-pass filters with a Kerr microcomb-driven transversal filter, so its link to the unitary-circuit theme is indirect. What is new is the joint emphasis on depth-efficient parameterization, modular tiling of unitary elements, and multifunctional use across computation, measurement, and filtering.

ranked.headline: Coupling sign, non-Hermiticity and edge modes tune flatband and BIC physics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report exact mobility edges, coupling-sign control of flatband formation, and antihelical edge states in photonic platforms.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the engineering of localized and confined optical modes in photonic platforms, with flat bands and bound states in the continuum as the dominant theme. Three of the four preprints address this directly. In C2-symmetric photonic-crystal slabs, a four-mode non-Hermitian model shows that coupling sign controls BIC merging and flatband formation, with Q scaling as k^-6. In one-dimensional non-Hermitian pseudospin lattices, non-Hermiticity is shown to embed compact localized states within a continuum. An experimental preprint realizes exact mobility edges and flat-band states in a two-dimensional photonic quasicrystal using auxiliary subsystems and photonic waveguides. The fourth item, a proposal for antihelical gapless edge states in a photonic metacrystal with staggered bianisotropy, addresses edge states rather than flat bands. What is new is explicit tuning of flatband and BIC physics through coupling sign and non-Hermiticity, together with experimental verification of exact mobility edges.
